name: Spain: participant-facing document QC
source: https://trialagents.com/ctis/spain/en/patient-facing-document-qc-checklist (reviewed 23 September 2026), with the rules of the linked Spain population guides
note: Run on the final Spanish versions that will be uploaded to CTIS, not only on the English master. Section ids follow the Germany structure so C8.11 is the no-instruction check named in conventions/template-instructions.md; source_section gives the Spain QC page section.
item_format: Each result records the item id, the outcome, a short rationale and evidence (quoted passage and source locator) or an explicit gap.

items.check: Study title, protocol code, sponsor and EU trial number are the same as in the application.
The document title clearly identifies the population or use case.
Site and investigator fields are correctly completed or intentionally left as controlled placeholders for site completion.
The introduction states that participation is offered in a research study that has received the required CEIm and AEMPS review, and invites the person to read, ask questions and consult others.
Study purpose, intended population, total planned participant number, treatments, treatment groups and the chance of receiving each option match the protocol; no full inclusion and exclusion list.
States whether the study medicine is authorised and whether its use is within the authorised indication.
Benefits described only when supported; states that the participant may receive no health benefit; free medicine, tests, results and closer follow-up are not presented as benefits.
Main effective treatment alternatives listed, including not joining; says so if the same medicine may be available in normal care.
Treatment after the trial: whether and under what conditions the study treatment may remain available.
Contacts: study doctor name, service, telephone and availability; urgent issues directed to usual or emergency care; participants told to disclose participation elsewhere and carry any trial card.
New information affecting willingness to continue will be communicated promptly; circumstances in which the sponsor or investigator may stop participation and follow-up that continues are explained.
No statements carried over from another protocol, country, cohort or study phase.
Treatment groups, allocation ratio, blinding, placebo, dose, route, schedule and treatment duration match the current protocol.
Number and timing of visits, remote contacts, hospital stays and follow-up match the protocol; total participation period with treatment and follow-up separated.

All trial-specific procedures (optional procedures, biopsies, imaging, genetic tests, digital tools, home nursing, medical-record review) are described and each marked as routine care or research-specific where relevant.
Contraception, pregnancy testing, breastfeeding and pregnancy follow-up match the protocol, without requirements absent from it.
items.applies_when: participants or their partners could become pregnant

items.check: Risk section reconciled with the IB or SmPC and the protocol: most frequent and most serious risks without an exhaustive technical list; unknown risks acknowledged; procedure-related risks not omitted.
Participant responsibilities: attending activities, reporting adverse events and medication changes, consulting the study doctor before changing medicines or herbal products except in an emergency.
Home activities, digital tools, travel to another site or access to medical records are explained.
items.applies_when: any decentralised element or record access

items.check: After a protocol change, every affected participant document has been reopened, not only the main adult form.
Every mandatory trial activity is distinguished from optional research; a participant cannot decline a protocol-essential procedure while apparently consenting to the main trial.
Optional substudies, future data use, future sample use and recontact each have a separate yes or no decision.
Refusing an optional activity does not imply withdrawal from the main study.
Optional boxes are not preselected and each choice has the correct signature logic.
Withdrawal wording does not require a signed revocation form; if the protocol has one, the PIS and the form say withdrawal remains valid without signing it.

Withdrawal distinguishes leaving trial visits, withdrawing trial consent and withdrawing optional future-use consent, and explains what happens to data and samples (no use in later analyses after withdrawal unless another lawful route or new consent applies).
Participation is voluntary; refusal does not affect care; consent can be withdrawn at any time without penalty or loss of the normal relationship with the treating team.

The consent form confirms that the participant read the PIS and the data-protection appendix, could ask questions, received enough information, understood voluntariness and agrees, without repeating the information sheet.

A population matrix from the protocol and recruitment plan exists; every group that may be enrolled or followed has a distinct, appropriate document pathway (see requirements.json population_sets); populations are mutually exclusive within each consent stage.

Transition points covered: adult consent at legal adulthood; consent before continuing when an adult regains capacity; information as soon as possible and consent or ratification after emergency enrolment.

Healthy volunteers: no expected therapeutic benefit stated; reason for healthy volunteers; full burden (confinement, fasting, blood volume, restrictions with periods); first-in-human uncertainty and safeguards; handling of screening findings.

Adults unable to consent: accessible participant information with support to consent personally where possible; representative or person connected by family or factual relationship identified with basis; prior instructions checked; objection and non-verbal resistance respected; re-consent when capacity returns.

Emergency enrolment: used only when the protocol and CEIm-approved documents contain the pathway; Article 35 and Royal Decree 1090/2015 article 7 conditions; family consultation; what already happened versus what continues; consent or ratification; right to object to use of data.
Impartial witness: only for a capable participant unable to read or write; witness impartial and unrelated to the study; AEMPS witnessed-consent form; witness records the participant's own choices.

Pregnancy: the main PIS has the pregnancy section; the pregnant partner of a male participant has her own specific consent document; infant data have the parent or guardian route; follow-up has a defined endpoint.
Optional future data and sample use has its own choice or document (see C6).
An optional substudy for a defined subpopulation has a separate information and consent document; a substudy open to all is a separate section of the main PIS with a yes or no choice.
The AEMPS Annex VIIIA personal-data appendix is present inside the document and is at most two pages.
Sponsor and site roles identified accurately: the site controls identifiable medical-record data; the sponsor receives coded trial data.
Legal basis and purposes explained; legally required trial processing is not presented as depending on an optional GDPR consent.
Confidentiality and authorised access to identifiable information explained.
Retention: 25-year sponsor and investigator retention and site record retention.
Participant rights and limitations, and data-protection contacts.
Result publication, data sharing and international transfers outside the EEA.
items.applies_when: data shared or transferred outside the EEA

items.check: Direct-data service activities (travel, reimbursement, home services) described by purpose; names of service companies not required.
No promise of deletion where retention is required; withdrawing from visits is not said to remove data already collected.
Optional future data use beyond the drug development programme or for unrelated diseases has its own choice, separate from processing needed for the authorised trial.
PIS/ICF, protocol, laboratory manual and S1 (AEMPS Annex XIII information) reconciled.
Sample type, quantity, collection schedule, mandatory or optional status and risks for every sample.
Analysis locations, responsible entity, coding, storage, retention, access and transfers.
What happens to remaining samples after the trial: destroyed unless the participant agrees to storage and future research.
If stored, the applicable Spanish biobank, registered collection or foreign repository model is identified with its location where available.
Future use, recontact and return of findings follow the participant's choices; withdrawal of sample consent is operationally possible (destruction or anonymisation) and its limits are explained.
Genetic testing checked separately: trial objective, exploratory or optional; the participant's choice about receiving validated, health-relevant findings where applicable.
Trial-purpose sample text follows AEMPS Annex VIIIB and sits preferably in the general PIS/ICF.
Data and samples have separate future-use choices; no bundled consent to any future research.

sections.title: Spain-specific checks: minors, costs, compensation and insurance

items.check: Parents who retain parental authority or the legal representative give prior consent.

If one parent signs, the other parent's express or tacit agreement is documented with the AEMPS wording: both parents signed, the other parent does not object, or the signer is the sole legal guardian.
Child under 12: whether the child has sufficient judgment to be heard is addressed and information is adapted to the child's understanding.
Every participant aged 12 or older has a separate age-appropriate information and consent path with their own signature, in addition to parent or representative consent.
Trial medicines and trial-specific procedures are free; no added cost beyond normal care.
Reimbursement and compensation match the financial budget: amount or method, payment route and proportional payment when participation ends early.
If compensation is offered: the AEMPS tax warning (compensation is income for Spanish tax purposes) is included and the amount does not create undue influence.
Insurance wording matches the actual Spanish insurance route (Annex VA, VI or VII) and Royal Decree 1090/2015, promises no broader coverage, and gives a usable contact for insurance questions.
Version and date in the document and the CTIS entry agree.
Version references inside the consent form match the information sheet.
CTIS receives blank participant forms: no participant names, signatures, personal email addresses or other unnecessary personal data.

The use copy has signature and date fields for the correct people: participant and investigator for standard adult consent; different fields for parent, representative, witness and emergency pathways.
Every signer receives the relevant information before signing; the participant or representative receives the PIS and a signed and dated copy.
Optional choices are tied to the person entitled to make them.
Handwritten name, signature and date fields as in the AEMPS model.
Representative basis or relationship field present where relevant.
Correct CTIS section (L, K) and naming convention; no version or date in the CTIS title.
Page numbering present.

No drafting instruction remains in the final version (italic notes, [bracket] and <<double-angle>> notes, ........... gaps, yellow [INSERT/IF/CHOOSE/NOTE] labels); fields completed by hand at consent stay blank.
Spanish text is natural and uses terminology a participant can understand.
No unexplained abbreviations, technical protocol language, repeated risks or long legal passages; random allocation, blinding and placebo explained.
AEMPS limits: at most 15 pages including the ICF; Arial or Times New Roman at 11 pt or larger; line spacing at least 1.5; margins not reduced.
A simple visit table instead of the protocol schedule where a table helps.
Contact details, emergency instructions and alternative treatments are easy to find.
Tested with a person who was not involved in drafting.
Translations reviewed by a qualified person and matching the approved source.
items.applies_when: document is adapted from a reference document in another language

items.check: Every participant-facing document is in Spanish and appears under the correct CTIS country and category.
Recruitment materials intended for potential participants are included.
The final set contains no conflicting versions.
The participant document list matches the protocol's population matrix and the Spain Part II package checklist.
